| [LIT-031](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-031.md) | Moving away from lexicalism in psycho- and neuro-linguistics | Krauska et al. (2023), DOI-10.3389/flang.2023.1125127. Standard production and comprehension models built on "lemmas" (stored triads of meaning, syntax and form, with syntax stopping at the word) inherit a lexicalist assumption that typology has refuted. Replacing that assumption needs new algorithms, not just new representations: separate meaning↔syntax and syntax↔form mappings with one integrated stage for retrieving and assembling syntactic structure.
